# `m.forex.previous_day_bar`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The previous UTC day's open, high, low, close, and volume of each currency pair.

```python
m.forex.previous_day_bar(symbols)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `TimestampStart` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Currency pairs, such as `C:EURUSD`; `dm.ALL` is refused, so use `m.forex.bars(dm.ALL, dm.Timespan.DAY).history(day, day)`. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `T`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." | REST |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the bar, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the UTC date of `TimestampStart` for an intraday or 1-day bar, and null for a bar that spans more than one date (several days, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses midnight). Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar's window, as an Instant. A bar of a day or longer starts at 00:00 UTC of its window's first day (a week's Sunday, a month's, quarter's, or year's 1st), whichever source serves it. A bar of a day or longer stamped at a time or on a day Massive is not known to use keeps that stamp, has a null `Date`, and ends one period after it, with a WARNING, since which day it covers is not known. Every other stamp, as each source sends it (quoted next), is moved there. From REST `t`: "The Unix millisecond timestamp for the start of the aggregate window." | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends its length after its start; a bar of a day or longer at 00:00 UTC after its window's last day. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Open` | double | The open price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `High` | double | The highest price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Low` | double | The lowest price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Close` | double | The close price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Volume` | double | The trading volume of the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Vwap` | double | The volume weighted average price. | REST |
| `Transactions` | long | The number of transactions in the aggregate window. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
